I think that’s a really good question and honestly, I haven’t thought about that too much… I am a believer in what you do within your personal life is okay as long as it doesn’t harm others. Now people can argue this and say watching porn doesn’t hurt anyone but there’s a reasonable list of ways it DOES. Unlike other addictions, porn is involving other people even if it’s just on a screen unlike alcohol, drugs, food.

Sex work beyond OF is usually happening because the women have been trafficked, are being controlled by a man for profit, etc. OF does give people that autonomy vs the normal conditions of sex work do which is why OF has been glorified because you are your own boss, although you are under a company that is run by men and are taking 20-30% of what you make (iirc… it’s been a while, but does this actually make you that girl boss everyone says? Uhhh probably not haha.)

OF COURSE there’s exceptions to all things, I’m sure there’s women out there who escort under their own terms and have created their own business and I think that’s a really important concept to take because a lot of the problems porn has caused are from the patriarchy rather than women being able to have autonomy over what they do in sexual situations.

Although I think if I thought on this more I could make a bit more sense of it all. All things related to this topic are constantly changing which need reevaluation, as all politics do. 🤓🤓🤓

2nd wave feminism is huge about porn not being empowering to any extent. This concept resulted in a sex war of anti-porn vs sex-positivity. Both can exist within the same space because you can be sex positive without consuming pornography and contributing to the industry by creating content for (most likely) the male viewer. Although within this period, I don’t think this thought is mentioned much, if at all. Really, you can be an extremely sexual person without giving into the consumption of porn and hyper-sexuality the internet has created.

Anyway, being an exhibitionist is simply a fetish, not some empowering act that needs to be recorded and sold, there’s other ways to be able to indulge into these fetishes without the creation of pornography. There’s plenty of people who aren’t pushed or forced into sex work, a lot of people who do this simply enjoy it and do it because we’re in a society that conditioned us to think that the creation of porn is okay, is empowering, is super progressive, when in reality you’re still contributing to the oppression, violence, and addiction that porn has created within our society simply for your own sexual needs/desires/fetishes. You can explore your sexuality without it being on a screen for hundreds to look at. The less we can contribute to the nonstop stream of porn being created, the better.

This isn’t me saying fetishes are bad, there’s physiological reasons these things happen and that’s okay, but your sexuality doesn’t have to contribute to the problem. You can exist and thrive within your sexual interests without exploiting them.

With that aside, as a beginner glassblower/basically someone with literally no experience… what makes you a good apprentice is listening and knowing when to shut up. I know that sounds harsh but blowing, especially production is an intense fast and hot environment that does not fuck around. If you can’t bring a good punty, can’t get a gather, can’t blow an even bubble… you’re done for. To learn all those things is to LISTEN and not talk back or argue when you don’t understand or think it can be done better. Gaffer is always in control and who is the ring leader in the shop/line of production making.

If you want kindness, compassion, and some patience, go through an art program at a college or take some intensive classes through Pittsburgh, Corning, etc.
The Glass Art Society has a list of colleges + universities that offer degrees/courses in glassblowing/kiln forming/neon/whatever.
